meta.description: Comprehensive citation management for academic research. Search OpenAlex, PubMed, and Google Scholar for papers, extract accurate metadata, validate citations, and generate properly formatted BibTeX entries. This skill should be used when you need to find papers, verify citation information, convert DOIs to BibTeX, or ensure reference accuracy in scientific writing.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabrication; emphasizes metadata validation and verification against multiple sources (CrossRef, PubMed, OpenAlex)

practice_boundaries.detail: Appropriate scope for citation management and bibliography generation; integration with scientific-schematics for diagrams shows clear boundaries

methodological_ground.detail: Based on established citation standards (BibTeX format) and authoritative sources (CrossRef, PubMed, OpenAlex)

code_usability.detail: Scripts documented with proper command-line interfaces; security warning about shell injection present

functional_suitability.note: Comprehensive coverage of citation workflow: discovery (OpenAlex/PubMed/Scholar), extraction (DOI/PMID/arXiv), enrichment, formatting, validation with venue standards

reliability.note: Excellent reliability: mandatory metadata enrichment phase, validation with exit codes, DOI verification, duplicate detection, incomplete field logging

performance_context.note: Well-organized with clear 4-phase workflow, reference files for detailed strategies, rate limiting guidance for Google Scholar

agent_usability.note: Excellent 'When to Use' with 10 specific scenarios; clear integration with literature-review and scientific-schematics skills; comprehensive workflow documentation

human_usability.note: Clear setup with Python 3.9+, dependency documentation, network access requirements, environment variables for rate limits, opt-in file writing

security.note: Exceptional security awareness: explicit shell injection warning with mitigation strategies (subprocess argument lists, quote escaping), citation key validation regex

maintainability.note: Good structure with version 2.0, license (MIT), comprehensive scripts directory; minor: changelog for version 2.0 not included

agent_specific.note: Strong composability with allowed-tools (WebSearch, WebFetch) and openclaw metadata; clear output formats; minor: idempotency of validation not explicitly documented

key_strengths: Exceptional security awareness with explicit shell injection warning and concrete mitigation strategies (subprocess lists, quote escaping, regex validation)
Outstanding workflow design with mandatory metadata enrichment phase (Phase 2.5) to address API incompleteness
Excellent multi-source strategy emphasizing OpenAlex and PubMed as primary sources with Google Scholar as supplement due to scraping fragility
Strong validation framework with exit codes, venue standards, manuscript checking, and DOI verification for CI/CD integration
Clear integration with complementary skills (literature-review for research, scientific-schematics for diagrams)

recommendations.title: Add safe vs unsafe command construction examples
recommendations.problem: Shell injection warning clear but no demonstrative safe/unsafe code comparison
recommendations.root_cause: Security guidance is textual without concrete code examples
recommendations.fix: Add example: Unsafe: os.system(f'grep {title} file'); Safe: subprocess.run(['grep', title, 'file'])

recommendations.title: Document venue reference count standards
recommendations.problem: Venue validation mentioned but specific standards not provided
recommendations.root_cause: references/validation_rules.md likely contains details but not shown in excerpt
recommendations.fix: Add note in main SKILL.md: 'Typical venue standards: Nature/Science ~50 refs, PLOS ONE no limit, Cell ~100 refs. See references/validation_rules.md for complete list.'
